summary: The StopSign-resync question is explained, but its leading upstream explanation, that the single max promise log merged at the prepare quorum can omit a StopSign carried by a losing promise, is still source-level. This revision tests it without changing the established observations. The seeded 900-action lossy run, reconfigure at action 450, 150-round fair-delivery convergence, node 3 trace, existing fields and the converged_all comparison are unchanged. Added diagnostics record every successfully delivered Promise addressed to pid 4 as sender, promise ballot number, accept round of its last accepted entry, accepted index, decided index and whether its log_sync carries a StopSign (up to forty entries), plus up to twenty accepted-index transitions on node 4 and its final accepted and decided indices. The prediction is concrete: if the max-merge explanation is right, node 4 should receive a StopSign-bearing Promise whose accept round is lower than a delivered Promise without the StopSign, and node 4's own accepted index should stay below the StopSign index while it still decides higher indexes. If instead the promises show no such ordering, the late-Promise path becomes the better explanation and the interpretation will be corrected again.
